summary: Short assistant-style requests covering 150 intents across ten everyday domains — travel, banking, work, small talk. One row is one written request and its intent. This corpus also ships an explicit out-of-scope class: those rows expect the engine to answer nothing at all, so a fighter that guesses on every input is punished here in a way the other intent corpora cannot punish it.
notes: CLINC150 (Larson et al. 2019) — 150 in-scope intents across 10 domains, English, plus an explicit out-of-scope class. Absorbed from ovos-intent-benchmark's dataset list. Uses the 'plus' config, whose 1000 out-of-scope test utterances are tagged bucket='far_ood' with expected_intent=None so the scorer treats a non-fire as correct — a genuine 'don't guess' regression test the other 3 absorbed corpora don't provide.
